The token floor evaluated at the iteration boundary (goal-auto.js:55 "const ITERATION_FLOOR = 80_000;" and :768 "if (budget.total && budget.remaining() < ITERATION_FLOOR) {"). Twelve lines. Only Synto does anything comparable, and it spends 175k tokens of self-rotation machinery to get there. Running out mid-iteration leaves a tree no gate has judged, which is precisely the state this design refuses to produce.

The draft PR opened at the first landed iteration and rewritten by each later one (goal-auto.js:744 "const published = await publish(shipping.pr ? 'edit' : 'create', facts, prBody(facts, issue), prBase);"). Every corpus file that opens a PR opens it at the end or not at all; a run that halts at 3 of 15 otherwise leaves a local branch nobody can see on a machine that is now asleep. Worth its ~35 lines because halting is the expected outcome here, not the exception.
prosecutor.sizeVerdict: Seven mechanisms have no equivalent anywhere in the corpus, and together they are roughly 470 of the 919 lines — more than double the corpus median for the whole script. Lenses (l.264-369, ~106 lines) pay an imagined risk by their own admission: the comment at l.261-263 concedes measured judge reliability is low, the stage is off by default (l.901), and it runs after `gh pr ready` so it can never change an outcome — a hundred lines that produce a comment nobody asked for. Tracks and self re-entry (l.477-546 plus l.562-604, ~113 lines) pay a real risk (independent workstreams serialized behind one lock) but currently pay it badly: the teardown promised at l.499 does not run when workflow() throws, so the expensive mechanism has the exact failure it was built to prevent. The remote control panel (l.409-462, l.694-700, ~60 lines) pays a real risk in its tier-1 form — a checkbox comment the run authored and reads back by id — but the tier-0 label path (l.435) is a second, redundant channel for the same three verbs and buys nothing tier 1 does not. The audit stage (l.371-407, ~37 lines) pays a real risk for its per-iteration cost record and an imagined one for \"which failures recur across runs\": that is speculative pattern-finding, delegated to a model, on a directory that will hold two files. PR mirroring (l.144-238 plus l.713-748, ~130 lines) pays a real risk — halting is the expected outcome, and an unpushed branch on a sleeping machine is the failure mode — though prBody/planFacts/quoted are the part doing the least work for the most fragility. Plan-hash pinning (~14 lines) and the token floor (~12 lines) pay real risks at negligible cost. Cut the lenses stage and the tier-0 label channel and the file loses ~130 lines while losing nothing that can change a run's outcome; spend a fraction of that on the retry budget, the transient/refusal distinction and the try/catch the corpus has and we do not.
